title: Session shaping by activity signals — jot
content:
Notes to self: want a compact, practical idea for reducing token spend by shaping session context using lightweight client-side activity signals. This is not a canonical PRD — more of a sketch for an experiment we can run on the hosted API and on Dedicated later.

Context / problem:
- Long-running sessions (chat, doc assist) accumulate a lot of context; often only a small subset is relevant to the current user action.
- Current TTL-based eviction or purely recency-based trimming wastes tokens on stale info; leads to higher cost and slightly higher latency.
- Teams want predictable cost savings without hurting response quality.

Hypothesis:
- If we weight context retention by simple activity signals (typing speed, scrolling, cursor focus, recent edits, explicit pin), we can reduce average context length by ~20–50% for many tasks without measurable quality degradation.

Key activity signals (client-observed, low telemetry cost):
1) Last input timestamp (active vs idle) — simple decay multiplier.
2) Typing burst intensity (chars/sec in last N seconds) — indicates in-progress work; increase retention.
3) Visible viewport / scroll position (last read range) — prioritize content in view.
4) Last edit location (doc cursor) — anchor locality for retention.
5) Explicit user pins / bookmarks — always keep.
6) Interaction count with a chunk (replies, highlights) — keep high-interaction chunks.
7) Short-term explicit user prompt types (question vs continue) — if question, keep Q/A context near prompt.

Heuristic rules (first pass):
- Partition session into numbered chunks (N tokens each or by turn). Each chunk has a dynamic score = base * activity_multiplier * recency_decay.
- base = importance inferred from chunk role (system messages = high, user messages = medium, assistant = medium-low unless referenced).
- activity_multiplier = 1 + alpha*(typing_burst_norm) + beta*(in_view_norm) + gamma*(edit_anchor_norm) + pin_flag*5
- recency_decay = exp(-lambda * minutes_since_chunk) with lambda tuned per product (chat vs doc).
- Evict lowest-scoring chunks until token budget hit.

Experiment design (MVP):
- A/B test on hosted API customers (opt-in) with sampling of chat-like sessions. Metric windows: 14 days.
- Control: current recency-only eviction with fixed token ceiling per session.
- Variant: activity-weighted eviction described above.
- Primary metric: average tokens consumed per session (delta downward is good).
- Secondary metrics: end-to-end latency (+/-), user-visible quality measured by a small synthetic eval (human raters on held-out sample), error rate (timeouts, hallucination proxy?), retention of pinned messages.
- Guardrail: automatic roll-back if quality drop > 2% on raters or user complaint rate spikes.

User stories / acceptance criteria:
- As a chat user, I should not see answers that omit recently edited context near my cursor. (Test: craft prompts that require the nearby edit to answer correctly.)
- As a doc assistant user, the assistant should prefer content visible on-screen for follow-up questions.
- As a power user who pins context, pinned items never get evicted.
- For offline or privacy-conscious clients, the signals can be computed client-side; only the resulting chunk score is sent as metadata (no raw viewport content).

Instrumentation & data needs:
- Need telemetry for tokens-per-session, chunk evictions, per-signal distributions (typing rates, in-view frequency).
- Add flags to request logs: chunk_scores_pre_eviction, chunks_evicted_count, tokens_after_eviction. Keep low-cardinality.
- Synthetic eval harness: create 100 canonical sessions per product (chat, doc) with labeled golden responses and perturbations to test omits/regression.

Rollout plan (fast path):
1) Local simulator: implement scoring & eviction in serving runtime simulator; run on trace log corpus to estimate token savings and worst-case omissions.
2) Internal dogfood: route a fraction of internal sessions through variant; collect telemetry + human QC.
3) Public beta: opt-in for selected customers; share expected savings and opt-out.
4) Gradual default with throttled rollout and rollback triggers.

Edge cases & risks:
- Malicious clients could mark everything as 'pinned' or fake activity signals; need server-side sanity checks and quota enforcement.
- For accessibility scenarios (screen readers, slow typers) scoring might penalize valid users — incorporate user-level fallbacks and slower decay for flagged accessibility accounts.
- Multidevice sessions: signals from device A may conflict with B; merge rules needed (OR vs weighted recency).

Open questions / TODOs:
- alpha/beta/gamma initial values? propose alpha=0.8, beta=1.2, gamma=1.0 as starting point (tunable).
- Chunk granularity: token-fixed (e.g., 256 tokens) vs turn-based — simulator should compare.
- Stability: how often to recompute scores per request? every request seems fine but may add CPU. Consider caching scores for 10s.
- Opt-in UX: how visible should this be to customers? Tag as "context shaping" in Console if enabled.
- Compliance: make sure viewport/typing signals are not stored long-term; document retention policy.

Example mock flows (sketch):
- User is editing paragraph 3, types question referencing the paragraph. Client sends request with chunk_scores metadata: chunk_1:0.2, chunk_2:0.9, chunk_3:2.7(pin false, edit_anchor true, in_view true, typing_burst high). Server keeps chunk_3 and recent assistant turns, evicts chunk_1.

Quick notes on implementation surface area:
- Client SDK: tiny API to compute and attach per-chunk signal summary (one-liner compute).
- Server: scoring module, eviction policy module, logging. Add config knobs in Console for lambda and per-team budgets.
- Console: show projected token delta per team/hr if enabled.

Next steps (short list):
- Build a simple scoring prototype in Python and run on 10k session traces (owner: me; due 2/28).
- Sync with Evan (runtime metrics) and Maya (dogfood program) this week; set up slack thread.
- Draft a lightweight internal explainer + safe-mode rollout proposal for product review.

Quick brainstorm ideas (parking lot):
- Combine with semantic anchors: if a chunk has a named anchor that matches current prompt, bump score massively.
- Use cheap embedding-similarity (64-d) as a tie-breaker for medium-scored chunks. Compute at ingest time.
- Offload heavy scoring to Dedicated tier where customers want deterministic retention.

Random scribbles: keep it simple initially; avoid heavy client instrumentation; aim for 15–30% token reduction for doc-edit workflows.

End of jot.

-- Samira
(Notes: share this with runtime-experiments and product-hosted-api; flag privacy and accessibility teams early.)
